title: Add six_seven() alias - this hits different fr fr 🔥
description:
## Summary

Added `six_seven()` as an alias for `slice_sample()` and ngl this slaps 💯

"Six seven" is peak Gen Alpha brain rot - it's literally just random noises that went viral (shoutout Skrilla's "Doot Doot" and LaMelo Ball). No meaning, just vibes. Perfect match for random sampling fr fr no cap.

## Changes

- ✨ New `six_seven()` function that wraps `dplyr::slice_sample()` 
- 📖 Updated README translation table with the new function
- 💡 Added example usage showing how to use it
- 📚 Added "Six seven" to the slang glossary (bussin documentation)
- 🎯 Full roxygen2 docs included

## Examples that go hard

```r
# Take a random sample of 8 rows
mtcars |> six_seven(n = 8)

# Take a random 25% sample and vibe check the columns
mtcars |>
  six_seven(prop = 0.25) |>
  vibe_check(mpg, cyl, hp)
```

## Vibe check

- [x] Function implementation matches the package style (simple wrapper, no extra sauce)
- [x] Roxygen2 docs are clean and concise
- [x] README updated with translation and examples
- [x] Slang glossary updated
- [x] No tests needed (just vibes)

This feature is absolutely bussin and ready to merge periodt 🔥✨

title: added in say_less() for n_distinct()
description:
Yo team 👋
Droppin’ a lil function called say_less() into the mix — it’s basically n_distinct() from dplyr, but with less typing and more vibe. Think of it as the TL;DR of counting unique stuff.
🧠 What it do:
- Wraps n_distinct() so you can count distinct values without breaking a sweat.
- Keeps your pipes clean and your code aesthetic.
- Syntax so minimal it’s practically a whisper.

title: find a value's oomfs
description:

Maybe oomf is too millennial in origin though 🙃
